generated_by: hand (the authored side of tools/dungeon_relics.py; the room kit reads nothing here)
why: The rewards behind the secrets (docs/mechanics/DUNGEON_PASS2.md, replayability 2). Every room that carries a secret also carries params.relic (an id, unique in the dungeon) and params.lore (one or two sentences, under lore_max characters; params.relic_name overrides the name made from the id). At the secret's relic spot a pedestal stands; a member who steps up to it is given the relic ONCE, for good: the guard is an advancement criterion on the player (cobblers:dungeons/relics/<short>, one criterion per relic), so it survives a death, a logout, the slot's reset and every later run. A criterion granted sets the player's count (dg.rl_<short>); the last one completes the advancement, which is the collection. The relic is a keepsake: an item no bank, counter or buyer prices, named and lored, no CobbleDollars, nothing sold. The slot's reset puts the pedestal back; it never touches the record.
rung: datapack plus generator: an advancement per dungeon, a score per dungeon, and per-room functions merged into the kit's tick and reset hooks. No mod, no scripting layer.
trigger_radius_why: measured from the pedestal's centre at feet level: the spot beside it (1.0) and the cells diagonal to it (1.41) are inside, a cell two away (2.0) is not. problems() proves no cell a player can reach without the secret's trick is inside, from the built grid
